key_insight: The paper shows that reinforcement learning can improve an LLM’s oncology treatment planning by learning from partially verifiable, patient-specific rewards rather than relying only on fully correct answers.
clinical_relevance: This approach may better support real-world cancer decision support, where multiple treatment paths can be reasonable and clinicians must first gather information before choosing a therapy.
method: Formulated colon cancer treatment planning as an interactive RL task under partial observability.
Built process-aware rewards from real-world clinical records to score information gathering, reasoning, and treatment selection.
Optimized Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with GRPO and GDPO and compared performance against frontier models.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, the GDPO-trained policy improved Mean@3 scalar clinical reward by 79.60% over base Llama and outperformed GPT-5.2 by 18.82% in the same interactive environment.
watch_item: Results come from an interactive evaluation environment, so clinical deployment would still require careful validation for safety, generalizability, and real-world workflow fit.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning
